findings.message: https://credentialengineregistry.org/resources/ce-5e3de882-3b49-421b-b623-695c63587f4f asserts ceasn:isChildOf but https://credentialengineregistry.org/resources/ce-177f4c85-4efe-401d-acdd-1ea4adeeaf37 does not assert the declared inverse ceasn:hasChild. One direction alone is not an error.

rule.citation: ceasn:isChildOf declares owl:inverseOf ceasn:hasChild in the schema encoding: if A ceasn:isChildOf B is asserted, then B ceasn:hasChild A must hold wherever both directions are stated.

findings.message: Referenced entity is a ceasn:CompetencyFramework, which the declared range of ceasn:isChildOf does not include, but Credential Engine's own guidance and examples use exactly this pattern.

rule.citation: Conflicting authoritative sources: the CTDL-ASN schema encoding does not list ceasn:CompetencyFramework in schema:rangeIncludes of ceasn:isChildOf, but the ceasn:isPartOf usage note instructs top-level statements to use isChildOf, and the CTDL Handbook's own examples point isChildOf at the framework. Reported as INFO, not an error, because the sources disagree.
